_comment: Weather data sources, fallback order and request settings. The 'probes' list is rewritten by scripts/probe_sources.py; everything else is edited by hand. response_source is the value written to the 'source' field of the spec IV.3 response and must be one of open_meteo, gdps, era5_climatology, snapshot_cache.

request.refresh_ttl_source: spec IV.8: weather responses cached 30 min
request.forecast_days_note: The skill horizon is 10 days of lead. 12 days are requested so that every stored forecast hour is inside the range of both ensembles and holds a value.
request.run_metadata_rule: A model run time reported by a metadata endpoint is accepted only if it is not in the future and the same record's data_end_time has not passed. A record whose own data has ended describes an old run; the fetch time is then stamped instead and issue_time_basis says so. The rule uses the record's own fields and no tolerance of ours.

ensemble.basis: docs/02_WORKFLOW_WEATHER.md, W3: 'a 1-member "probability" is not a probability'. Two members is the smallest ensemble. In operation the ensembles have 51 and 31 members.
ensemble.require_complete_members_note: A forecast is used only if every member has a value for every evaluated field at every hour of the window. A forecast with a missing value is not used and the date is answered from climatology; no member is dropped to make a forecast fit.

chain_notes: probability() walks the ensemble chain for every row except the supplement fields, then the ensemble_supplement chain for those, and falls to era5_climatology if either cannot answer. No single open ensemble carries every field (probed 2026-10-03, 11 models): only the ECMWF ensembles carry low and mid-level cloud cover, and only NCEP GEFS and the UKMO global ensemble carry visibility. The deterministic chain serves fetch_forecast() for single-run forecasts; a single run never yields a probability.

data_defects.finding: Open-Meteo returns 0.0, not null, for the convective precipitation field 'showers' in every one of the 87,672 hours of the ERA5 archive (2016 to 2025) and in every member and hour of the ECMWF IFS ensemble. Total precipitation in the same data is non-zero in 20.3 percent of archive hours. The field is therefore not usable, and a non-null check alone does not detect this.
data_defects.consequence: criteria_v1 evaluates no row on 'showers'; its lightning proxy is CAPE-based. The archive builder drops any field that is constant over the whole period and reports it, and a test asserts that every evaluated field varies.

data_defects.field: cape, visibility, wind_speed at pressure levels (Open-Meteo ERA5 archive)
data_defects.finding: Null in the ERA5 archive as served by Open-Meteo. Visibility is also null in the ECMWF IFS ensemble.
data_defects.consequence: CAPE is read from the NSF NCAR copy of ERA5 instead. Visibility is read from the ECCC station observation. ERA5 pressure-level winds are not obtainable without the Copernicus key within a practical time (57 s per level per day on the NCAR server), and no numeric upper-level wind limit is published, so upper-level winds are not a criterion.

open_meteo_ecmwf_ens.description: ECMWF IFS ensemble, 51 members, as served by the Open-Meteo ensemble API
open_meteo_ecmwf_ens.licence: Open-Meteo free tier is for non-commercial use; data CC BY 4.0.

open_meteo_gefs_ens.description: NCEP GEFS ensemble, 31 members, 0.5 degree, as served by the Open-Meteo ensemble API. Supplies visibility, which the ECMWF ensemble does not carry.
open_meteo_gefs_ens.licence: Open-Meteo free tier is for non-commercial use; data CC BY 4.0. Underlying data: NOAA NCEP, public domain.

open_meteo_gfs.description: NCEP GFS deterministic forecast as served by the Open-Meteo forecast API
open_meteo_gfs.licence: Open-Meteo free tier is for non-commercial use; data CC BY 4.0.

open_meteo_gdps.description: ECCC GEM global deterministic forecast (GDPS) as served by the Open-Meteo forecast API
open_meteo_gdps.licence: Open-Meteo free tier is for non-commercial use; data CC BY 4.0. Underlying data: Environment and Climate Change Canada.

snapshot_cache.description: The most recent forecast held on disk: backend/weather/cache/ (written on every live fetch) or backend/weather/data/snapshot/ (committed for the offline demo). It keeps its original forecast_issue_time.

climatology_archive.description: Hourly archive for the Canso grid point: ERA5 reanalysis for every model field, and the station observation for visibility, which no reanalysis carries.
climatology_archive.licence: Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information (ERA5). Visibility: Data Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada. Open-Meteo free tier is for non-commercial use.
climatology_archive.period_note: first_year to last_year are the complete calendar years the climatology is built from. They start in 2022 because that is the first complete year of the archive used to fill gaps in the station visibility record. Through the Copernicus route the archive also extends past last_year to the latest published day, so that recent forecasts can be verified; those extra months do not enter the climatology.
climatology_archive.selection_rule: Three ways to the same reanalysis. 'open_data' (default of the committed archive): surface fields from the Open-Meteo ERA5 archive; CAPE from Copernicus when CDSAPI_KEY holds a real token and the download packages are installed, otherwise from the NSF NCAR ERA5 archive, which needs no key but publishes months late, so without a key the archive ends at last_year. 'era5_cds': every ERA5 field from Copernicus, month by month, which is the route issue #3 W4 names as preferred and takes hours in the Copernicus queue. 'auto': era5_cds when the key is usable, else open_data. Visibility comes from the station in every case.

era5_cds.description: ERA5 hourly reanalysis from the Copernicus Climate Data Store, single levels. An alternative route to the same ERA5 fields the open route provides; used when CDSAPI_KEY holds a real token.
era5_cds.credential_location: environment variables, or backend/weather/.env (ignored by git); template in backend/weather/.env.example
era5_cds.python_packages_note: Needed only by the archive download script, not at run time. pyproject.toml is owned by API and does not list them: pip install cdsapi xarray netCDF4.
era5_cds.snowfall_note: ERA5 gives snowfall in metres of water equivalent. It is converted to centimetres of snow with the factor Open-Meteo applies, so that both acquisition paths share one definition. The factor is UNVERIFIED against Open-Meteo's source and is immaterial here: the criterion only tests for non-zero snowfall.
era5_cds.licence: Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information. The ERA5 licence must be accepted once on the CDS website.
era5_cds.status: Verified against the live service on 2026-10-04: one month downloaded with the owner's key, parsed, and compared hour by hour with the open route (see backend/weather/progress.md).
era5_cds.precision_note: Precipitation and snowfall water equivalent are rounded to 0.1 mm, the precision of the forecast data the criteria are evaluated against. Found necessary against a real download on 2026-10-04: unrounded ERA5 precipitation was non-zero in 328 hours of April 2024, against 162 at 0.1 mm precision.
era5_cds.latency_note: ERA5 is published with a delay of about five days (preliminary ERA5T). Requests stop this many days before today so that no unpublished day is asked for; any hour still unpublished is trimmed from the end.
era5_cds.request_size_note: Copernicus refuses large requests. On 2026-10-04 a request for one quarter of ten variables was answered '403 cost limits exceeded. Your request is too large', while one month of ten variables was served. The full route therefore asks month by month; CAPE alone is asked in half years.

open_data.description: ERA5 without a key: surface fields from the Open-Meteo archive API with models=era5, and CAPE from the NSF NCAR ERA5 archive (dataset d633000) through its THREDDS NetCDF Subset Service.

era5_cape.note: Open-Meteo returns null for ERA5 CAPE, so CAPE is read from the NSF NCAR copy of ERA5 (ECMWF parameter 128.059), one request per month, anonymous access.

station.note: The nearest ECCC station that reports hourly visibility. HART ISLAND (AUT), 3.5 km from the site, reports none. Probed 2026-10-03.

gap_fill.note: Hours the station did not report are filled with the NCEP GFS visibility at the Canso grid point from the Open-Meteo historical forecast archive. Every filled hour is listed in the archive metadata under gap_filled.

climatology.source: issue #3 W4: any bin with fewer than 30 samples is flagged low_confidence

forecast_source.description: Archived individual runs of the NCEP GFS deterministic model, four per day, as served by the Open-Meteo single runs API
forecast_source.first_run_date_note: Earliest run the archive returned when probed on 2026-10-04; runs of 2025 and earlier answer 'The requested model run is not available'.
forecast_source.licence: Open-Meteo free tier is for non-commercial use; data CC BY 4.0. Underlying data: NOAA NCEP, public domain.

hindcast.ensemble_construction: The four runs initialised on one UTC date form a four-member time-lagged ensemble for that issue date. The forecast probability for a lead is the fraction of those runs that satisfy every criterion over the evaluation window of the valid date, computed by the same function as the operational layer.
hindcast.why_not_the_operational_ensembles: No open archive keeps past runs of the ECMWF or GEFS ensembles in a form that can be read without a GRIB decoder: the Open-Meteo ensemble and single runs APIs answered 'not available' for every past ensemble run probed on 2026-10-04. The hindcast therefore verifies the criteria and the forecast chain on GFS runs, not the operational 82-member probability.
hindcast.require_all_runs_note: An issue date with fewer than four runs in the archive is excluded and counted.
hindcast.lead_max_days_source: spec III.4 protocol: 'generate daily P(L | d) from archived forecasts for leads 1-10 days'. This is the range the hindcast scores. It is separate from the operational FORECAST boundary in skill_horizon.json, which the hindcast measures.
hindcast.aggregate_leads_source: spec III.4 pass criterion 1: BSS aggregated over leads 1-7 days

fixture.date_basis: backend/fixtures/weather.json is the API's offline record. The API tests request it for 2026-10-06 (backend/api/tests/test_client.py, test_cache_and_limits.py) and the frozen window rows in backend/fixtures/windows.json are centred on that date. It is three days after the issue time of the committed forecast snapshots, inside the FORECAST boundary.

supplement.rule: p_launch = max(0, P_primary - Q), where P_primary is the fraction of primary members that satisfy every row the primary carries, and Q is the fraction of supplement members that satisfy every row both ensembles carry and violate a supplement row.
supplement.why: The two ensembles are separate samples, so the joint behaviour of a cloud row and visibility inside one member is not available. The rule uses no dependence assumption: P(A and B) = P(A) - P(A and not B) >= P(A) - P(common rows hold and not B). The reported value is therefore a lower bound that equals the exact member fraction whenever no supplement member fails on a supplement row alone. It can only understate the launch probability, never overstate it.
supplement.measured: In the 2022 to 2025 archive visibility was the only violated row on 1.6 percent of days; on 94.7 percent of the days with reduced visibility another row was violated as well.
